claims.statement: @forceorg/types is a dependency-free, header-only contract package whose main/types both resolve to src/index.ts: it supplies the cross-layer vocabulary (datasheet, wargear AST, roster, audit, sync, and ApiResponse shapes) consumed with `import type` by apps/api, apps/web, apps/sync-worker and @forceorg/rules-engine-11e, and therefore contributes no runtime code.

The HTTP contract is the ApiResponse envelope — success boolean plus optional data, error.code/error.message, and a pagination meta block (page/totalPages/totalCount); docs/OPENAPI.yaml splits it into ApiSuccess (success=true, data required) and ApiError (success=false, error.code+message required, code drawn from a fixed enum of eleven values), and meta is only emitted in practice by GET /api/datasheets.

Every response surface in apps/api conforms to the envelope: the rate limiter (429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED), requireAuth (401 UNAUTHORIZED/TOKEN_INVALID), each router handler's try/catch (400 INVALID_PARAMS/NO_FILE, 404 NOT_FOUND, 500 DB_ERROR/UPLOAD_ERROR/DELETE_ERROR/AUDIT_ERROR), the terminal 404 middleware, and the global error handler (500 INTERNAL_ERROR).

apps/web/src/lib/api.ts is the only in-repo envelope consumer: apiFetch throws ApiError(error.code || 'UNKNOWN') when !response.ok || !body.success and otherwise returns body.data cast to T with no runtime validation and discards meta, so a route that breaks the envelope fails only at the type level in the client.

GET /api/changelog never returns 500: on a database failure it answers HTTP 200 with success:true, the curated CURATED_BALANCE_CHANGES constant and syncStatus 'OFFLINE', so clients must branch on syncStatus rather than success to judge data freshness; its syncStatus ternary is degenerate ('SYNCHRONIZED' on either branch) and 'PENDING' is never produced anywhere.

The ruleset version id format is 11.1.0-YYYY-QN-MFM and generateRulesetVersionId() in apps/sync-worker/src/etl-pipeline.ts is its only generator, computing year and calendar quarter from the current date at run time; its value is written solely to SyncMetadata.rulesetVersionId (once per endpoint, so all rows of a run share it, including NO_DELTA and ERROR rows).

Outside the worker the ruleset version is a hardcoded literal in two non-matching families: '11.1.0-2026-Q3-MFM' in the changelog route fallback/offline branch and in the web changelog page and ComplianceDashboard, and '11.1.0-2026-Q3' (no -MFM) in the roster create route, the audit route's rulesetVersionCompared, docs/API.md, and every web offline/starter-army fallback in lib/api.ts, app/page.tsx, app/army/[id]/page.tsx, app/army/[id]/edit/page.tsx and CreateArmyModal.tsx.

No roster row ever receives a worker-generated ruleset id: POST /rosters hardcodes UserArmy.rulesetVersionId to '11.1.0-2026-Q3' (ignoring any client-supplied value) and the audit labels its result with the same frozen string while comparing stored points against live datasheets_11e rows — so a real MFM points change appears as a POINTS_SHIFT discrepancy attributed to the wrong ruleset, and currentRulesetVersion from /changelog can never string-match army.rulesetVersionId.

BattlefieldRole, WargearRuleType, TargetRole, AbilitySource, BattlePhase and StratagemCategory exist as compile-time string-union type aliases in packages/types/src/index.ts and as runtime Prisma enums in schema.prisma (re-exported as values from @forceorg/db-client and materialised as Postgres CREATE TYPE in the init migration), with a third inline mirror in docs/OPENAPI.yaml — so adding or renaming a label requires a coordinated schema + migration + types + OpenAPI + seed + UI change that no build step enforces.

The duplication extends to model names (Datasheet, UserArmy, Ability, Stratagem, SyncMetadata, UserUnitMedia, LeaderCompatibility) exported with materially different fields by @forceorg/types and the Prisma client — Date vs ISO string, Json vs typed composition/stats — and the API bridges them with `as unknown as` casts, so field drift between the two is invisible to the type checker.

Enum-valued catalog tables (datasheets_11e, weapons_11e, abilities_11e, stratagems_11e, wargear_rules_11e, leader_compatibility_11e) carry no RLS — public read with writes reserved for the sync-worker service role — while the RLS-isolated tables (user_armies, user_unit_media, user_color_schemes) hold no enum columns, so enum drift can only enter through the worker/seed write path and never through a tenant write.

UserArmy.rosterPayload is a bare Prisma Json column written verbatim by POST /rosters (defaulting to {units:[],totalPoints:0,detachmentPointsUsed:0}) and PUT /rosters/:id with no runtime validation anywhere in the repo, which makes the RosterPayload/RosterUnitInstance interfaces in @forceorg/types the only schema of record for it; OpenAPI marks only instanceId, datasheetId, datasheetName, modelCount and pointsCost required.

The audit and rules engine depend on specific RosterUnitInstance fields: audit.ts casts the JSON to RosterPayload and reads units[].datasheetId (datasheet existence and POINTS_SHIFT comparison of pointsCost vs Datasheet.basePoints), while validateRoster consumes totalPoints, detachmentPointsUsed, datasheetId (Rule of Three counting) and attachedLeaderId/instanceId (orphan-attachment detection); a malformed payload throws inside the handler and surfaces as a generic 500 AUDIT_ERROR.

Two roster unit encodings coexist in the same JSON column: RosterBuilder persists its local RosterUnit (nested catalogUnit, validationErrors, and wargearSelections using `optionId` where WargearSelection declares `selectedOptionId`) from the edit page's auto-save, while offline/guest mode in lib/api.ts writes the lean typed shape — forcing view mode to define an OfflineRosterUnit normaliser that defaults battlefieldRole to 'INFANTRY' when catalogUnit is absent.

RosterUnitInstance.instanceId is a logical join key only: user_unit_media references it as a plain VarChar(64) with a @@unique([rosterId, unitInstanceId]) constraint and no foreign key, so renaming the field or rewriting payloads silently orphans stored miniature photos.

The sync contract is weaker than the catalog one: @forceorg/types narrows SyncMetadata.status to SUCCESS|NO_DELTA|ERROR|PENDING while the schema stores an untyped VarChar(30) (the worker writes only SUCCESS, NO_DELTA and ERROR), and SyncDelta is defined but effectively dead — etl-pipeline.ts imports analyzeDiff/formatChangelogSummary without calling them, so GET /changelog reports curated changes rather than analysed deltas.
